title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: Which of the following expressions is never a prime number when \(p\) is a prime number?

solutions.text: Look at \(p^2 + 26.\) When \(p = 3,\) it’s \(35 = 5 \cdot 7.\) For any other prime, \(p\) isn’t divisible by \(3,\) so \(p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 3\) and \(p^2 + 26 \equiv 1 + 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 3.\) Either way it’s a multiple of \(3\) bigger than \(3,\) hence composite. So it’s never prime. Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Test the expressions modulo \(3;\) for a prime \(p \ne 3,\) \(p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 3\)
For the correct choice, also check \(p = 3\) separately, then show it is a multiple of \(3\) for all other primes
